title: Fire Mage / Fury Warrior / Holy Paladin vs Jungle
summary: A machine-drafted plan for Fire Mage / Fury Warrior / Holy Paladin into Feral Druid, Beast Mastery Hunter and Discipline Priest — kill target, control allocation and cadence are derived from cooldowns and defensive counts; the order is a guess. Correct it on any step.

sections.title: Kill target: the Discipline Priest — and the trade-off
sections.body:
Count the personal defensive cooldowns each of the three holds: the Feral has four (Barkskin, Frenzied Regeneration, Survival Instincts, the trinket), the Priest has four (Fade, Desperate Prayer, Pain Suppression, the trinket), and the Hunter has six (Aspect of the Turtle, Camouflage, Exhilaration, Roar of Sacrifice, Survival of the Fittest, the trinket). The Hunter is out on count alone.

Feral and Priest tie on count, and an earlier version of this plan broke the tie with an argument that does not hold up. It said that killing the healer ends the enemy's sustain while killing the Feral 'only removes one source of their damage', as though a dead Feral left a functioning team behind. It does not. In three-versus-three, killing any of the three usually ends the round — a Hunter and a Priest with no Feral are not playing on, they are losing slowly. Treating the healer as the only kill that counts is a habit, not an analysis, and it is worth naming because it has quietly shaped most of the plans on this site.

With that argument removed, the case for the Priest is narrower and more honest: this comp's damage arrives in one stacked window rather than as sustained pressure, and a Discipline Priest is the member of their team least able to survive a single window without help, because the help is her. That is a real reason. 'Killing the Feral would not end the game' was not.

The trade-off is still live, and it now runs the other way more often than the first version admitted. The Feral is where the enemy's control lives — Maim, Cyclone, the roots, Typhoon — and he is also the target who most often dies to exactly the kind of burst this comp does, because he has to stand in melee to function. If he is the one in reach when the window comes up, take him. The plan below is written for the Priest; it is not an instruction to ignore a Feral standing in the middle of your Combustion.

Because the Priest is both the healer and the kill target here, the usual four roles collapse to three: there is no separate 'control the healer' step — holding the Priest and killing her are the same action, covered next — and both remaining enemies need cross-CC, since either one can peel for her.

sections.title: Hold the Priest — she's also the kill target

steps.note: Closes the gap and lands the opener in the same action, so the stun isn't delayed by a run-in.
Locks her down before anything commits — break it with the first hit of the burst, not before.
The one that actually holds through the burst — it's the only category here that doesn't break on our own damage.

NOT on the Priest. Storm Bolt and Hammer of Justice are both 30-second stuns in the same category, so spending them back-to-back on one target halves the second one for nothing. Send this one at the Feral or the Hunter instead — two separate full-duration stuns on two players beats one and a half on one, and both are back before the next attempt.

sections.title: Cross-CC the Feral and the Hunter — either one can peel

steps.note: A frontal cone — catches both if they're stacked on the Priest. If they're spread, it only gets one, and this plan has no way to know which.
The long root, not the short one — spend it on whichever of the two Blinding Light missed.

Every third beat this arrives already stacked with Recklessness and Bladestorm — see cadence.

Avenging Crusader is the same talent — one choice node, not a second cooldown — and this plan takes Wrath because the comp is trying to close a game inside a window, not heal through one.

This is the real save for the Priest, not a personal defensive — it reduces damage taken by an ally. If it lands on her mid-go, expect the burst to underperform even with no trinket used.

sections.title: Cadence: a 30-second beat that scales up
sections.body:
The shared beat is 30 seconds. Storm Bolt, Hammer of Justice, Meteor, Pyroblast, Heroic Leap and Divine Toll are all back on that cycle, so a real attempt — a stun plus the Mage and Paladin's reliable damage — is available every 30 seconds regardless of what else is up.

Every second beat (60s) Combustion joins. Every third beat (90s) the Warrior's whole heavy kit — Avatar, Bladestorm, Champion's Spear, Recklessness — arrives together; it's already self-aligned inside one player, without needing anything else to line up. Every fourth beat (120s) Avenging Wrath joins on top of all of it, which is the biggest window this comp has.

Shockwave, Dragon's Breath and Ring of Frost all sit on their own tier (40s) that lines up with neither the 30-second rhythm nor Combustion's 60 — treat them as opportunistic, not scheduled.

Missing the beat costs more than the ability spent. If Storm Bolt goes out off-cycle, the next stun on the Priest arrives without Meteor, Pyroblast or Divine Toll lined up behind it, and the go that was meant to land inside Avenging Wrath's window instead arrives early, without it.

sections.title: Where this is guessing
sections.body:
1. Positioning isn't in this data at all. Blinding Light catching both Feral and Hunter, and Charge reaching a third target, both assume they're stacked near the Priest. If they're spread, cross-CC collapses to one target and the other peels free — a real player will know how these three actually position, this plan doesn't.

2. The kill target. Feral and Priest tie on defensive count. This plan picks the Priest for the sustain-denial upside, but the Feral is where the enemy's own control lives — which is actually right depends on how pinnable each of them is in practice, and this plan has no way to judge that.

3. SETTLED. An earlier version of this plan agonised over whether to hold Hammer of Justice or chain it diminished behind Storm Bolt, and both options were wrong. Two 30-second stuns in one comp are not a chain and should never be spent on the same player — one goes on the healer and one goes on a damage dealer, every 30 seconds, and both land at full duration. The plan above now does that.

The related point, also settled: Polymorph is not a third link here. This comp's damage is spread and largely periodic, so a Polymorph cast during a go breaks almost immediately — it is a reset tool between attempts, not cross-CC inside one.

4.Whether Roar of Sacrifice landing on the Priest mid-go should end the attempt or not. This plan assumes a partial go still forces something worth having — a spent Sacrifice, maybe a trinket — even without a kill, but it doesn't prove that's the right call here.
